rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths took refuge in the mountain cave to flee their people while preserving their religion; they asked God for mercy from Him and guidance toward the right course.
rows.anchor: فقالوا إذ آووه: {ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة} [الكهف: 10] رغبة منهم إلى ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their request for a rightly directed course means that God make easy what pleases Him and their escape from disbelief and idol worship, and guide them to sound action.
rows.anchor: يسر لنا بما نبتغي وما نلتمس من رضاك والهرب من الكفر بك، ومن عبادة الأوثان

rows.speaker: عمرو
rows.claim: The youths followed Jesus, while their idolatrous king pressed them to worship idols; they refused and withdrew to a cave to protect their faith.
rows.anchor: قال: ثنا عمرو، في قوله: {أصحاب الكهف والرقيم} [الكهف: 9] كانت الفتية على دين عيسى على الإسلام

rows.speaker: عمرو
rows.claim: One youth proposed his father's cave as refuge; the people sealed them inside, then a later Christian king removed the barrier, whereupon they awoke and estimated they had slept a day or part of one.
rows.anchor: فقال أحدهم: إنه كان لأبي كهف يأوي فيه غنمه، فانطلقوا بنا نكن فيه

rows.speaker: عمرو
rows.claim: The youths sent one of their number to Ephesus with an old coin; the townspeople recognized its age, consulted the king and records, and rejoiced when they learned the youths' story.
rows.anchor: ثم أخرج درهما، فنظروا إليه فأنكروه، وأنكروا الدرهم، وقالوا: من أين لك هذا؟

rows.speaker: عمرو
rows.claim: When the envoy returned to the cave with the people, God caused the youths to sleep again, and the people proposed building a place of worship over them.
rows.anchor: فقال الذين غلبوا على أمرهم: {لنتخذن عليهم مسجدا} [الكهف: 21]

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq relates that Christian belief had weakened amid sin and idolatrous rulers; Deqianus persecuted those who retained Jesus' religion, forcing the faithful to flee or face death and mutilation.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: مرج أمر أهل الإنجيل وعظمت فيهم الخطايا وطغت فيهم الملوك

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: The young nobles sought God's help through prayer, fasting, charity, praise, and tears as persecution intensified; they were freeborn youths from prominent Roman families.
rows.anchor: وكانوا فتية أحداثا أحرارا من أبناء أشراف الروم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reports that at least one youth still showed a downy beard because he was so young.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: لقد حدثت أنه كان على بعضهم من حداثة أسنانه وضح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they were eight, naming Mكسلمينا as the eldest and the one who spoke to the king, followed by the other named youths.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فكانوا كذلك في عبادة الله ليلهم ونهارهم يبكون إلى الله، ويستغيثونه، وكانوا ثمانية نفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As Deqianus prepared a citywide sacrifice to idols, the youths prayed for the believers' deliverance; informers found them prostrate and reported their disobedience to the king.
rows.anchor: اللهم رب السماوات والأرض، لن ندعو من دونك إلها {لقد قلنا إذا شططا} [الكهف: 14]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king summoned the eight tearful, dust-covered youths and demanded that they sacrifice to his gods or be killed.
rows.anchor: اختاروا مني: إما أن تذبحوا لآلهتنا كما ذبح الناس، وإما أن أقتلكم

rows.speaker: مكسلمينا
rows.claim: Their spokesman declares that the Lord of heaven and earth alone is their God; they will worship and ask help only of Him, never idols or devils.
rows.anchor: فقال مكسلمينا: إن لنا إلها نعبده ملأ السماوات والأرض عظمته، لن ندعو من دونه إلها أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deqianus strips the youths of their rank and jewelry but postpones punishment, giving the young men time to reconsider their refusal.
rows.anchor: فإني سأؤخركم أن تكونوا من أهل مملكتي وبطانتي وأهل بلادي، وسأفرغ لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing the king's return, each youth takes money from his father's house, gives some away, and sets out for a nearby mountain cave; their dog follows.
rows.anchor: أن يأخذ كل واحد منهم نفقة من بيت أبيه، فيتصدقوا منها، ويتزودوا بما بقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They devote themselves to worship in the cave and entrust their provisions to Yemliha, who secretly enters town disguised as a poor man to buy food and learn news.
rows.anchor: وجعلوا نفقتهم إلى فتى منهم يقال له يمليخا، فكان على طعامهم، يبتاع لهم أرزاقهم من المدينة سرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Deqianus returns to Ephesus and orders sacrifices, Yemliha reports that the youths have been found and are sought, alarming his companions.
rows.anchor: فأخبرهم أن الجبار دقينوس قد دخل المدينة، وأنهم قد ذكروا وافتقدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths prostrate themselves, pray for protection from persecution, and eat the small meal Yemliha brought as evening falls.
rows.anchor: فرفعوا رءوسهم، وأعينهم تفيض من الدمع حذرا وتخوفا على أنفسهم، فطعموا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After their meal and conversation, God puts them to sleep in the cave for many years while their dog lies at its entrance and their provisions remain with them.
rows.anchor: إذ ضرب الله على آذانهم في الكهف سنين عددا، وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه بباب الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deqianus searches for the missing youths and tells the nobles he would have forgiven them if they repented, but the nobles urge him to question their parents and punish them.
rows.anchor: فألقى الله عز وجل في نفسه أن يأمر بالكهف فيسد عليهم كرامة من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspires Deqianus to seal the cave to honor and preserve the youths' bodies until their revival as a sign of resurrection; two secret believers record their names and story on lead tablets in a sealed copper chest.
rows.anchor: وأراد أن يحييهم ويجعلهم آية لأمة تستخلف من بعدهم، وأن يبين لهم أن الساعة آتية لا ريب فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two secret believers, Bedros and Ronas, record the youths' names, lineages, and story on lead tablets in a sealed copper chest by the cave, hoping future believers will find them.
rows.anchor: اسم أحدهما بيدروس، واسم الآخر: روناس، فأتمرا أن يكتبا شأن الفتية أصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the youths were noble sons who gathered unexpectedly; their eldest voiced belief in the Lord of heaven and earth, the others agreed, and all decided to enter the cave.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: كان أصحاب الكهف أبناء عظماء مدينتهم، وأهل شرفهم، فخرجوا فاجتمعوا وراء المدينة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reports that they slept in the cave for three hundred and nine years under the tyrant Deqianus.
rows.anchor: فلبثوا في الكهف ثلاثمائة سنين وازدادوا تسعا رقدا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: They were richly dressed young princes who encountered one another while leaving a festival where their people carried idols; each had independently received faith from God and feared persecution.
rows.anchor: عن عبد العزيز بن أبي رواد، عن عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير، قال: كان أصحاب الكهف فتيانا ملوكا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: The youths cautiously paired off to test one another's beliefs, discovered that all shared faith, and entered a nearby cave with their hunting dog, where God made them sleep for 309 years.
rows.anchor: فإذا هم جميعا على الإيمان، وإذا كهف في الجبل قريب منهم، فقال بعضهم لبعض: ائتوا إلى الكهف

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Their people searched for them but could not find the cave; they later recorded the youths' names and lineage, and a Muslim king succeeded the earlier ruler after generations passed.
rows.anchor: كتبوا أسماءهم وأنسابهم في لوح: فلان ابن فلان، وفلان ابن فلان أبناء ملوكنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported explanation says they fled a ruler's pursuit after one of them was accused of committing a crime.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل كان مصيرهم إلى الكهف هربا من طلب سلطان

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb relates that a disciple of Jesus converted young nobles while working at a bath; after the king's son and a woman died there, the blamed disciple and youths fled with a farmer and dog, slept in a cave, and were sealed inside by the king.
rows.anchor: قال: أخبرني إسماعيل بن شروس، أنه سمع وهب بن منبه، يقول: جاء حواري عيسى ابن مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about striking their ears means that God put them to sleep, as the idiom of striking someone with paralysis means afflicting him with it; the years are counted and the accusative is explained by the verb.
rows.anchor: بالفالج، بمعنى ابتلاه الله به، وأرسله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God awakened them so people could determine which of the two disputing groups most accurately calculated the period they had slept; amad means the endpoint or term.
rows.anchor: لينظر عبادي فيعلموا بالبحث، أي الطائفتين اللتين اختلفتا في قدر مبلغ مكث الفتية

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the two groups as parties from the youths' own people.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، {أي الحزبين} [الكهف: 12] من قوم الفتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some authorities say both groups among the people were unbelievers; others say one group was Muslim and the other unbelieving.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم: كان الحزبان جميعا كافرين. وقال بعضهم: بل كان أحدهما مسلما، والآخر كافرا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says neither group, whether unbelievers or believers, knew the youths' duration of sleep.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله {ثم بعثناهم لنعلم أي الحزبين أحصى لما لبثوا أمدا} [الكهف: 12] يقول: ما كان لواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet al-Nābigha uses amad for the goal or limit reached in a race.
rows.anchor: سبق الجواد إذا استولى على الأمد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses amad as something distant or long in duration.
rows.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله {لما لبثوا أمدا} [الكهف: 12] يقول: بعيدا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses amad as a number or count.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، {أمدا} [آل عمران: 30] قال: عددا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative amad is best read as an explanatory specification of ahsa, meaning which group most accurately counted their duration, because exegetes support this interpretation.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو أولى الوجهين في ذلك بالصواب، لأن تفسير أهل التفسير بذلك جاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative parses amad as the object of labithu, giving the sense of the endpoint of their stay.
rows.anchor: والآخر: أن يكون منصوبا بوقوع قوله {لبثوا} [الكهف: 12] عليه، كأنه قال: أي الحزبين أحصى للبثهم غاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Muhammad the truthful account of the youths who took refuge in the cave after the Meccan pagans asked about them; they believed in their Lord.
rows.anchor: الذين سألك عن نبئهم الملأ من مشركي قومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God increased their faith and insight, enabling them to endure leaving home and comfortable life for hardship in the cave to preserve their religion.
rows.anchor: وزدناهم إلى إيمانهم بربهم إيمانا، وبصيرة بدينهم، حتى صبروا على هجران دار قومهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspired patience and strengthened their hearts with the light of faith, so that they could give up their former comfort.
rows.anchor: وألهمناهم الصبر، وشددنا قلوبهم بنور الإيمان

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains that their hearts were strengthened through faith.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {وربطنا على قلوبهم} [الكهف: 14] يقول: بالإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths spoke to Deqianus when he reproached them for refusing his gods; their Lord owns the heavens and earth, whereas his idols are created beings, so they would not worship them.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا إله غيره، وإن كل ما دونه فهو خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling on any god besides the Lord of heaven and earth would be an outrageous, exaggerated falsehood that exceeds the bounds of truth.
rows.anchor: لقد قلنا إذن بدعائنا غيره إلها شططا من القول: يعني غاليا من الكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the idiom for bidding, shatata means to exceed the proper measure; distance and height have different forms of the root.
rows.anchor: يقال منه: قد أشط فلان في السوم إذا جاوز القدر وارتفع

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited poet's phrase ashatat witnesses the sense of exceeding the proper limit.
rows.anchor: ألا يا لقومي قد أشطت عواذلي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses shatata as a lie.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله {لقد قلنا إذا شططا} [الكهف: 14] يقول كذبا

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses shatata as erroneous speech.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله {لقد قلنا إذا شططا} [الكهف: 14] قال: لقد قلنا إذن خطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths tell one another to leave their people, who worship gods besides God, and take refuge in the cave so that God may spread mercy and ease their situation.
rows.anchor: وإذا اعتزلتم قومكم الذين يعبدون من الآلهة سوى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase about what their people worship, ma is accusative and coordinated with the pronoun suffix in iʿtazaltumuhum.
rows.anchor: إذ كان ذلك معناه في موضع نصب عطفا لها على الهاء، والميم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada notes that Abdullah's codex reads wa-ma yaʿbuduna min dun Allah, clarifying that the people worshipped other than God.
rows.anchor: وهي في مصحف عبد الله: «وما يعبدون من دون الله» هذا تفسيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marfiqan means something by which the youths can find ease or support in their distress and fear for faith and life.
rows.anchor: ويهيئ لكم من أمركم مرفقا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra reports both vowel patterns for marfiq in the hand and in the sense of a useful thing.
rows.anchor: وكان الفراء يحكي فيهما، أعني في مرفق الأمر واليد اللغتين كلتيهما

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i accepts only the pattern with fatha on fa and kasra on mim for the elbow.
rows.anchor: إلا فتح الفاء وكسر الميم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra reports both forms for the arm joint and for a beneficial thing, and cites a rajaz line using marfiq and mirfaq.
rows.anchor: وكان الفراء يحكي فيهما، أعني في مرفق الأمر واليد اللغتين كلتيهما

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The rajaz poet's pairing of marfiq and mirfaq illustrates the two forms.
rows.anchor: بت أجافي مرفقا عن مرفقي

rows.speaker: نحويي أهل البصرة
rows.claim: A Basran grammarian treats marfiqan as a noun meaning a useful thing, patterned like masjid, or as a form meaning ease.
rows.anchor: شيئا ترتفقون به مثل المقطع، ومرفقا جعله اسما كالمسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both regional readings are valid and equivalent, but he prefers the Iraqi kasra-mim, fatha-fa reading as the more eloquent and common Arabic form.
rows.anchor: فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فمصيب. غير أن الأمر وإن كان كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazawwar means that the rising sun turns or leans away from the cave, from the root for crookedness or turning aside.
rows.anchor: من الزور: وهو العوج والميل

rows.speaker: بشر بن أبي خازم
rows.claim: Bishr ibn Abi Khazim's verse uses izwirar to mean turning away or avoidance.
rows.anchor: يؤم بها الحداة مياه نخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most Medinan, Meccan, and Basran readers double the zay, while most Kufans read it lightly; both forms are established and close in meaning.
rows.anchor: فقرأته عامة قراء المدينة ومكة والبصرة: (تزاور) بتشديد الزاي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some also transmit tazur with a light initial t and geminated r, and tazwar in the pattern of tahmar.
rows.anchor: وروي عن بعضهم: «تزور» بتخفيف التاء وتسكين الزاي وتشديد الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both well-known readings, with light or doubled zay, are correct; the two rarer variants are linguistically possible but too anomalous to read.
rows.anchor: لشذوذهما عما عليه قرأه الأمصار

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr glosses tazawwar as turning or leaning.
rows.anchor: عن سالم الأفطس، عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: {وترى الشمس إذا طلعت تزاور عن كهفهم ذات اليمين} [الكهف: 17] قال: تميل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sun leans away from the youths on the right at sunrise and on both sides as it passes.
rows.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، {تزاور عن كهفهم، ذات اليمين} [الكهف: 17] يقول: تميل عنهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains that the sun inclines rightward and leaves the youths untouched on that side.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وترى الشمس إذا طلعت تزاور عن كهفهم ذات اليمين} [الكهف: 17] يقول: تميل ذات اليمين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says direct exposure would have burned them, and without being turned from side to side the earth would have consumed them.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، قال: لو أن الشمس تطلع عليهم لأحرقتهم، ولو أنهم لا يقلبون لأكلتهم الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At sunset the sun leaves the youths on the left; by passing away from both sides it avoids striking them, which otherwise could burn or bleach them.
rows.anchor: وإذا غربت الشمس تتركهم من ذات شمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basran Arab usage takes qarada as cutting past and leaving something behind; the Kufans instead explain it as being opposite or alongside.
rows.anchor: وأما الكوفيون فإنهم يزعمون أنه المحاذاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root qarada means cutting, as in cutting cloth, scissors, or a mouse gnawing fabric.
rows.anchor: وأصل القرض: القطع، يقال منه: قرضت الثوب: إذا قطعته

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's line uses yaqriḍna to mean that the camels cut across or pass through the route.
rows.anchor: إلى ظعن يقرضن أجواز مشرف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the sunset clause as leaving the youths untouched.
rows.anchor: ثني معاوية، عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وإذا غربت تقرضهم ذات الشمال} [الكهف: 17] يقول: تذرهم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the sun leaves them on the left at sunset.
rows.anchor: عن سالم الأفطس، عن سعيد بن جبير، قال {وإذا غربت تقرضهم} [الكهف: 17] تتركهم ذات الشمال

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses taqriḍuhum as leaving them.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قول الله عز وجل: {تقرضهم} [الكهف: 17] قال: تتركهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada also explains the sunset clause as leaving the youths alone on the left.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {وإذا غربت تقرضهم ذات الشمال} [الكهف: 17] يقول: تدعهم ذات الشمال

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the setting sun leaves the youths on the left; Sa'id ibn Jubayr gives the same gloss, leaving them.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {تقرضهم ذات الشمال} [الكهف: 17] قال: تدعهم ذات الشمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fajwa means an open, spacious area within the cave; its plural forms are fajawat and the extended fajāʾ.
rows.anchor: {وهم في فجوة منه} [الكهف: 17]

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses the cave's fajwa as an open space.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {وهم في فجوة منه} [الكهف: 17] يقول: في فضاء من الكهف

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains fajwa as the inner place of the cave.
rows.anchor: عن سالم الأفطس، عن سعيد بن جبير، {وهم في فجوة منه} [الكهف: 17] قال: المكان الداخل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses it as a remote or far-off place.
rows.anchor: عن منصور، عن مجاهد، {وهم في فجوة منه} [الكهف: 17] قال: المكان الذاهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance and misguidance are in Gods hands; whoever is misled will find no ally to guide him to the truth.
rows.anchor: لأن التوفيق والخذلان بيد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad should not grieve over his people's rejection, since guidance and misguidance belong to God, who could have guided them if He willed.
rows.anchor: فلا يحزنك إدبار من أدبر عنك من قومك وتكذيبهم إياك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sleepers would look awake to an observer; ayqaz is the plural of yaqiz, as illustrated by a rajaz verse, while ruqud is plural of raqid like julus and quʿud.
rows.anchor: والأيقاظ: جمع يقظ، ومنه قول الراجز

rows.speaker: الشاعر الراجز
rows.claim: The rajaz poet uses ayqazan as the plural of yaqiz and supports the lexical explanation.
rows.anchor: ووجدوا إخوتهم أيقاظا … وسيف غياظ لهم غياظا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God turns the youths during sleep onto their right sides and then their left sides.
rows.anchor: ونقلب هؤلاء الفتية في رقدتهم مرة للجنب الأيمن، ومرة للجنب الأيسر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says this turning occurred in their first sleep and reports that Abu Iyad said they were turned twice each year.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ونقلبهم ذات اليمين وذات الشمال} [الكهف: 18] وهذا التقليب في رقدتهم الأولى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that without the turning the earth would have eaten them.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، {ونقلبهم ذات اليمين وذات الشمال} [الكهف: 18] قال: لو أنهم لا يقلبون لأكلتهم الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes differ over the dog: some say it was their actual dog, while another account identifies the figure as a human cook who followed them.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم: هو كلب من كلابهم كان معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Qatada, and Dahhak gloss wasid as the cave's courtyard or forecourt; Ibn Jurayj says it guards the cave entrance.
rows.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {بالوصيد} [الكهف: 18] يقول: بالفناء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A separate transmission from Ibn Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr says wasid means the ground or open earth.
rows.anchor: يعني فناءهم، ويقال: الوصيد: الصعيد

rows.speaker: عمرو
rows.claim: Amr also explains wasid as the ground or open earth.
rows.anchor: الحكم بن بشير، عن عمرو، في قوله: {وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه بالوصيد} [الكهف: 18] قال: الوصيد: الصعيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses wasid as the door.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، {وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه بالوصيد} [الكهف: 18] قال: بالباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers wasid to mean the door or its threshold, where the dog guards the cave, because the word is related to closing a door.
rows.anchor: قول من قال: الوصيد: الباب، أو فناء الباب حيث يغلق الباب، وذلك أن الباب يوصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasid is the Tihami and Yemeni dialect form alongside Najdi asid, paralleling other dialect pairs with initial waw or hamza.
rows.anchor: وفيه لغتان: الأصيد، وهي لغة أهل نجد، والوصيد: وهي لغة أهل تهامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who looked into the cave would flee in terror because God clothed the sleepers with awe, preventing anyone from reaching or touching them until their appointed awakening.
rows.anchor: حتى يبلغ الكتاب فيهم أجله، وتوقظهم من رقدتهم قدرته وسلطانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their awakening at God's chosen time makes them a sign that God's promise is true and the Hour is coming without doubt.
rows.anchor: حتى يبلغ الكتاب فيهم أجله، وتوقظهم من رقدتهم قدرته وسلطانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most Medinan readers use the doubled lam in la-mulliʾta, suggesting repeated filling with terror; Iraqi readers use a light lam, suggesting one filling.
rows.anchor: من قوله: (ولملئت) بمعنى أنه كان يمتلئ مرة بعد مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both widely transmitted readings are close in meaning and correct.
rows.anchor: وهما عندنا قراءتان مستفيضتان في القراءة، متقاربتا المعنى، فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فمصيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths question one another because they find their long sleep strange; some estimate a day or part of one, believing that is how long they slept.
rows.anchor: ظنا منهم أن ذلك كذلك كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The others defer the matter to God, saying that their Lord knows best how long they remained asleep.
rows.anchor: فقال الآخرون: {ربكم أعلم بما لبثتم} [الكهف: 19] فسلموا العلم إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths send one of their number to their former city, Ephesus, to buy food because they have awakened hungry.
rows.anchor: فبعثوا أحدهم بورق يشتري طعاما

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says a shepherd opened the cave for sheltering sheep from rain; the youths revived the next morning and sent one with old silver to buy food, revealing their long sleep to a righteous king.
rows.anchor: أنه سمع وهب بن منبه، يقول: إنهم غبروا، يعني الفتية من أصحاب الكهف بعد ما بني عليهم باب الكهف

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: When the messenger led the king and people to the cave, terror kept them from entering; they later built a church or mosque there for prayer.
rows.anchor: فبنوا عندهم كنيسة، اتخذوها مسجدا يصلون فيه

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reports that Christian youths, sons of Roman kings, withdrew from their people and slept until a Muslim community and king arose, then sought God's sign amid a dispute about bodily resurrection.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، عن عكرمة، قال: كان أصحاب الكهف أبناء ملوك الروم، رزقهم الله الإسلام

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: The awakened envoy's old coin exposed the era he came from, and the king presented the youths as a sign that body and soul are resurrected together.
rows.anchor: فهذا رجل من قوم فلان، يعني ملكهم الذي مضى، فقال الفتى: انطلقوا بي إلى أصحابي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says that when people entered the cave they found bodies without souls, and the king called them a sign from God.
rows.anchor: فإذا أجساد لا ينكرون منها شيئا، غير أنها لا أرواح فيها، فقال الملك: هذه آية بعثها الله لكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, passing the cave on campaign with Habib ibn Maslama, says the youths' bones had already vanished more than three hundred years later.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس، كان قد غزا مع حبيب بن مسلمة، فمروا بالكهف، فإذا فيه عظام

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq's account places the awakening under the righteous king Theodosius, whose reign lasted sixty-eight years and whose people split over belief in the Hour.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، فيما ذكر من حديث أصحاب الكهف، قال: ثم ملك أهل تلك البلاد رجل صالح يقال له تيذوسيس

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: The disputants included believers and deniers who claimed only souls, not bodies, would be raised and forgot scripture; falsehood gained ground over the believers.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من يكذب، فكبر ذلك على الملك الصالح تيذوسيس، وبكى إلى الله وتضرع إليه

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Theodosius withdraws, wears sackcloth, sits on ashes, and prays in grief for a sign to resolve the dispute.
rows.anchor: دخل بيته فأغلقه عليه، ولبس مسحا وجعل تحته رمادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God intends the youths' appearance to establish the Hour and bodily resurrection as truth, answer Theodosius' prayer, preserve his faith and rule, and gather dispersed believers.
rows.anchor: ثم إن الرحمن الرحيم الذي يكره هلكة العباد، أراد أن يظهر على الفتية أصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspires Olyas to remove the stones from the cave entrance for a sheep pen; terror keeps people at a distance while the youths sit up revived, greet each other, and pray unchanged.
rows.anchor: فاستأجر عاملين، فجعلا ينزعان تلك الحجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After prayer, the youths ask Yemliha what happened and estimate their sleep as a day or part of one; he says Deqianus seeks them and will force sacrifice or kill them.
rows.anchor: فقال لهم يمليخا: افتقدتم والتمستم بالمدينة، وهو يريد أن يؤتى بكم اليوم

rows.speaker: مكسلمينا
rows.claim: Maksalimina urges them to face death without abandoning belief in God or the life after death.
rows.anchor: فقال لهم مكسلمينا: يا إخوتاه اعلموا أنكم ملاقون، فلا تكفروا بعد إيمانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They instruct Yemliha to go secretly to town, learn what is said about them, and bring more food; he takes their old coins and sees the cave entrance has been unsealed.
rows.anchor: وأخذ ورقا من نفقتهم التي كانت معهم، التي ضربت بطابع دقينوس الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths think they have slept only their usual night and still believe Deqianus is seeking them, unaware that 309 years have passed.
rows.anchor: أن استيقظوا ثلاث مائة وتسع سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yemliha sees Christian signs displayed at the city gates and hears people openly invoking Jesus, unlike the persecution he remembers; the changed city leaves him bewildered.
rows.anchor: فرأى فوق ظهر الباب علامة تكون لأهل الإيمان، إذا كان ظاهرا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks a local youth the city's name and learns it is Ephesus, yet fears he has lost his mind and tries to leave unseen.
rows.anchor: فقال له: ما اسم هذه المدينة يا فتى؟ قال: اسمها أفسوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Yemliha offers an ancient coin for food, sellers pass it around and suspect he has found a buried treasure from long ago.
rows.anchor: ثم جعلوا يتطارحونها بينهم من رجل إلى رجل، ويتعجبون منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The townspeople accuse Yemliha of hiding a treasure, threaten to take him to the ruler, bind him, and parade him through the streets as a stranger.
rows.anchor: أخذوا كساءه فطوقوه في عنقه، ثم جعلوا يقودونه في سكك المدينة ملببا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They bring him to the city's two righteous governors, Arius and Astius; he believes he is being taken to Deqianus and cries to God for help.
rows.anchor: وهما رجلان صالحان، كان اسم أحدهما أريوس، واسم الآخر أسطيوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yemliha fears separation from his brothers and recalls their pledge never to forsake faith or one another in life or death.
rows.anchor: وقد كنا تواثقنا أن لا نفترق في حياة ولا موت أبدا
